## TL;DR

Close-out no longer keeps a worktree (or flips a Done card to Needs input) just
because the worktree contains the `.env` symlink RepoOS itself provisioned. The
shared dirty-worktree predicate (`uncommittedWorkFiles`) gained an opt-in
`ignoreProvisionedFromMain` option that drops untracked entries which are either
a symlink resolving into the main checkout or a path main's own ignore rules
already cover. Every close-out and handoff guard passes the main root, so the
predicate stays consistent across `/done`, the review/landability preflight, the
close-out cleanup, the restart dialog and the handoff drift checks. A real
uncommitted file still keeps the worktree and still names itself in
`needs_input`. Tests cover the symlinked `.env`, a path main gitignores, a
symlink outside main, a tracked modification, and the full cleanup path.

## Work and rationale

The reported state was a worktree whose removal had stalled half-way: tracked
files were gone from disk, `.gitignore` was gone with them, but the
RepoOS-created `.env` symlink survived. In that state `git status --porcelain`
reports ` D .gitignore` plus `?? .env`. Cleanup already discounts ` D` entries
that still exist at the branch ref (`omitWorktreeDeletionsPresentAtRef`), so the
leftover list collapsed to `.env` alone — and the orchestrator kept the worktree
and patched `needs_input: closeout-worktree-dirty` for a link the merge never
carried. Deleting that link loses nothing: its target is main's `.env`.

The key observation is that `.env` is normally invisible to this check. While
the worktree's committed `.gitignore` exists, `.env` is ignored and never
appears in `git status`; the link only becomes "uncommitted work" after the
stalled removal has destroyed the ignore rules. That is why the bug looked
intermittent and why a fix that special-cased the orchestrator alone would have
left the same false positive in the pre-close-out guards.

I put the fix in `uncommittedWorkFiles` (`src/core/git.ts`) behind a new
`ignoreProvisionedFromMain?: string` option rather than in one caller. The
function already owns the definition of "uncommitted task work"; adding the
main root there means callers cannot drift. The filter is deliberately narrow:

- Only untracked (`??`) entries are eligible. A tracked file's modification is
  always work, whatever the ignore rules say.
- A path is provisioned when it is a symlink pointing into the main checkout
  (`isSymlinkIntoMain`) or when `git check-ignore` run in the main checkout
  reports it. Both the resolved target and the link's literal destination are
  compared, so a dangling `.env` link still counts; main-root comparison handles
  macOS `/var` → `/private/var`.
- Failure is conservative: if `check-ignore` errors, nothing is discounted and
  the path stays counted as work.

Every "is there uncommitted task work?" call site now passes `config.root`: the
close-out cleanup, both close-out preflight functions, `POST /api/tasks/:id/done`,
the restart dialog's worktree-dirty endpoint, the pre-review remote gate, the
handoff snapshot comparison and the worktree-handoff guard. That keeps the
"RepoOS-provisioned paths are not task work" invariant single-sourced.

Tests: four table-driven cases on `uncommittedWorkFiles` (inherited `.env` plus
a real file, a path main gitignores, a symlink outside main, a tracked
modification) and a new end-to-end file that builds a real opted-in repo with
`ensureWorktree`, merges the branch, deletes `.gitignore` to reproduce the
stalled removal, and runs `CloseOutOrchestrator` cleanup. The first e2e case
asserts the pre-fix list is `[".env"]`, the filtered list is empty, the worktree
is removed, the branch is gone and no `needs_input` is written. The second adds
`real-work.txt` and asserts the worktree is kept, the file survives and the task
detail names it without blaming `.env`.

Docs were updated where the invariant lives: `docs/close-out-pipeline.md`
(worktree-cleanup invariant) and `docs/previews.md` (`inheritEnv`).

## Approaches tried

- **Fix only in `CloseOutOrchestrator.cleanup`.** Rejected: the same false
  positive would still block `repoos done` with `409 worktree has uncommitted
  files`, mark handoff drift, and show `.env` in the restart dialog.
- **Hard-code `.env` in the excluded list.** Rejected: narrower than the
  acceptance criterion, and RepoOS also provisions other links (candidate
  `node_modules`) and main may ignore other local files.
- **Use `git check-ignore -z`.** It requires `--stdin`, which `gitCapture` does
  not support. Newline-separated output is used instead; a path git has to
  C-quote simply fails to match and stays counted as work, which is the safe
  direction.
- **Treat every status entry as provisioned, not just `??`.** Rejected: a
  tracked symlink or file edit is real work and must block close-out.
- **Test at the predicate only.** Kept the predicate tests, but added the e2e
  cleanup test because the reported symptom (worktree kept, Done card Needs
  input) is produced two layers above the predicate.

## Challenges and blockers

Reproducing the bug required modelling the half-removed tree: in a normal
worktree `.env` never reaches `git status`. The e2e fixture opts the repo into
`[worktrees] inheritEnv` so the symlink is created by the real code path, then
deletes `.gitignore` after the merge to put the worktree in the state the
incident left behind.

The first scoped check failed on remote validation with two tests that are
unrelated to this diff: `agent-review.test.ts`'s land-anyway guard (its own
comment notes the full-suite-load race that widens the auto-bounce window) and a
`remote-host-pool` host-lock timeout. Both passed locally in isolation (the
host-lock test in 176 ms), and a re-run of the check was fully green. No changes
were made for them.

One small test-helper wrinkle: the fixture `git()` helper trims output, which
eats the leading space of porcelain's ` D` column, so the status assertion
compares the trimmed lines rather than the raw porcelain text.

## Key learnings

- "Untracked" is relative to the tree's ignore rules. A partially deleted
  worktree loses those rules, so files RepoOS provisioned become apparent
  leftover work — the failure mode here.
- Provisioned-vs-data needs an explicit, conservative predicate: symlinks into
  the main checkout and paths main ignores are safe to discount; anything
  unknown or tracked stays work.
- Keeping that predicate in `uncommittedWorkFiles` with an explicit main root
  means every guard (close-out, handoff, review, restart UI) agrees by
  construction instead of being patched one site at a time.
